author: Chris Cooley
name: Null Invaders
description: Fly an interceptor through a real webpage. Turn letters into binary, break the button factories, and clear the aliens they release.
versionNote: Four waves. One page. Increasing firepower.
controls: Mouse / WASD / arrows — fly and aim
P — pause · G — next factory · Esc — Recall

chapters.title: Every heading is cover. Every button is a factory.
chapters.body: Bullets travel through viewport space and collide with cached text geometry. A letter can be hit once: its original glyph is concealed and a 0 or 1 appears in the same place, matching the page’s font, weight and color. Button health drains through a liquid fill. A destroyed factory stops spawning for the rest of that wave.

chapters.title: Get stronger during the fight.
chapters.body: Pulse starts with one shot. Twin unlocks at 8 XP, Trident at 24, and four-shot Overdrive at 50. Letters give 1 XP, aliens 4, factory hits 2, and a destroyed factory another 8. Fire cadence accelerates from 160 ms to 95 ms. Weapon pods appear on the interceptor as it upgrades.

chapters.title: A tiny cast, built from pixels.
chapters.body: Three original alien silhouettes use two-frame animation. The interceptor gains weapon pods, engine flicker and a temporary shield. Art is baked into 15 × 16 canvas tiles and reused with image smoothing disabled. No image downloads, sprite DOM nodes or animation library.

chapters.title: Fast shots still hit thin letters.
chapters.body: A swept segment test checks the path from the previous bullet position to the next. The nearest intersecting glyph, alien or factory wins, so a fast projectile cannot simply jump across a narrow letter between frames. Alien and bullet objects are recycled through bounded pools.

extra: Three shields. Four waves. Factories reactivate between waves. Chained kills build a multiplier up to ×5; losing a shield resets the combo, but keeps your weapon.
